authoredSolutions.1: Only Faraday's law of induction carries a time derivative. \[\oint \overrightarrow{E} \cdot \overrightarrow{dl} = - \frac{\partial\phi_{B}}{\partial t}\] Under static conditions the magnetic flux does not change, the right-hand side vanishes and the relation collapses to \(\oint \overrightarrow{E} \cdot \overrightarrow{dl} = 0\), which is the separate electrostatic statement. Of the other equations, \(\oint \overrightarrow{B} \cdot \overrightarrow{dl} = \mu_{0}I\) is Ampere's law without the displacement-current term, so it holds only for steady currents, and \(\oint \overrightarrow{D} \cdot \overrightarrow{dA} = Q\) is Gauss's law, which holds in both regimes. The equation whose content belongs to time varying fields and not to statics is therefore Faraday's law, and the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.2: Read the four networks from the figures. In the first, two resistors in parallel are in series with a third; in the second, two in series are in parallel with a third; in the third all three are in parallel; in the fourth all three are in series. \[R_{A} = \frac{R}{2} + R = \frac{3R}{2}\] \[R_{B} = \frac{2R \times R}{2R + R} = \frac{2R}{3}\] \[R_{C} = \frac{R}{3}\] \[R_{D} = 3R\] Every network is fed by the same current \(I\), so the dissipation is \(P = I^{2}R_{eq}\) and the power rises with the equivalent resistance. \[\frac{R}{3} < \frac{2R}{3} < \frac{3R}{2} < 3R\] Hence \(P_{C} < P_{B} < P_{A} < P_{D}\), and the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.3: Each liquid column has real depth \(d/2\). The apparent depth of a column is its real depth divided by the refractive index of that column, and the two shifts simply add. \[d_{app} = \frac{d/2}{n_{1}} + \frac{d/2}{n_{2}}\] \[d_{app} = \frac{d}{2}\left( \frac{n_{2} + n_{1}}{n_{1}n_{2}} \right)\] \[d_{app} = \frac{d\left( n_{1} + n_{2} \right)}{2n_{1}n_{2}}\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.4: A magnetic field varies with time only when its source varies with time. Statement (A), a permanent magnet, and statement (C), a direct current, both produce steady fields. Statement (B) describes an electric field changing linearly with time, which gives a constant displacement current \(\varepsilon_{0}\frac{\partial E}{\partial t}\) and therefore a constant magnetic field. Statement (D), a decelerating charged particle, is an accelerating charge whose current changes with time, so it does generate a time varying magnetic field. Among the four combinations offered, only the one reading \(\text{(D) only}\) picks a genuine time varying source without also including a steady one, so the correct choice is A.
